subject.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:...] from wiping archive content

question: Should reset/deleted cron archives that lack session-store and record-level sessionKey provenance remain opaque, or may they become searchable to avoid all content-based false positives?
rationale: Current writer evidence contradicts the PR's assumption that all genuine cron JSONL records retain session keys, so the permanent boundary affects session recall and internal cron-output exposure.

options.title: Require durable provenance before merge
options.body: Add or prove a real writer-backed cron provenance path, or keep a narrow fallback that preserves orphan cron opacity without wiping human `[cron:]` conversations.

options.title: Accept searchable ambiguous archives
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally allow metadata-less cron archives to be indexed, but that should be an explicit security/session-state decision with tests documenting the tradeoff.

options.title: Pause for canonical branch selection
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers choose the landing path among the same-root fixes for the canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Require durable provenance before merge
recommendation.body: Add or prove a real writer-backed cron provenance path, or keep a narrow fallback that preserves orphan cron opacity without wiping human `[cron:]` conversations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent corpus and memory session sync work makes him the best available owner for the session provenance boundary.
